findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

Follow-ups are consumed under a fresh `command:<uuid>` that is never associated with the owning turn or persisted in its continuation payload. If the owner fails before replying, group-processing.ts:755 releases only `turn:<runId>`. Restart recovery likewise releases only that turn consumer, then marks pending continuations applied (live-execution.ts:689–698). Consequently, an accepted but unanswered follow-up remains consumed permanently. Persist recoverable ownership for these items and release unanswered continuation input on failure and recovery.
findings.title: Not done: No message is lost or given twice

findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

Recovery unconditionally releases every item consumed by the recovered run. A worker can deliver its reply and then crash before finalizing the live turn; the successor will release and process that already-answered input again. The recovery caller in runtime/live-turn-recovery.ts:141–144 does not distinguish whether output was delivered. This violates the covered requirement that failures after replying never give the messages again. Recovery needs durable delivery evidence before deciding which input to release.
findings.title: Preserve replied input when recovering a crashed worker

findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

Replacing command processing with an unconditional queue wakeup removes the active `/stop` and `/new` path. On the owning worker, GroupQueue.enqueueMessageCheck only sets pendingMessages while a run is active (group-queue.ts:226–229), so `/stop` cannot interrupt that run. On another worker, the continuation path recognizes only `/compact` (runtime-services-active-compact.ts:74), so `/stop` and `/new` are consumed and forwarded as ordinary model text. Preserve immediate authorized command dispatch while updating its consumption record.
findings.title: Restore active /stop and /new dispatch before queueing

findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

The new child processes call takeInput and getMessagesByIds directly, then exit. They never run admission processing, live-turn ownership, continuation delivery, a runner, or reply handling. The late message is saved only after both children finish. This proves repository claim exclusion, but would still pass if the runtime dropped every claimed message. Add the required two-worker runtime flow with an arrival during an active turn and assertions on actual delivery and remaining input.
findings.title: Not done: two-worker end-to-end no-loss/no-duplication test

findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

The claimed restart consists of constructing another repository over the same live database connection. Queue execution is mocked, and the test itself consumes the item afterward. No runtime restarts, no runner receives the message, and no consumed turn or pending continuation is recovered. It therefore cannot detect either lost follow-ups or duplicate replies after restart. Exercise an actual runtime restart against persisted input and assert delivery through the production recovery path.
findings.title: Not done: restart recovery test

findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

The failure proof here supplies outputSentToUser directly and checks calls to a mocked releaseInput. The group-processing tests also mock consumption; the Postgres tests exercise releaseInput directly without a failing runtime turn. These tests cannot establish that real delivery controls persisted consumption or that the next turn receives exactly the unanswered messages. Add runtime tests with a real database and failures before and after observable output, followed by another turn.
findings.title: Not done: failure-before-output and failure-after-output end-to-end tests

findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

The polling assertion uses takeInput with consumedBy='history' to check whether input remains. If the runtime leaves an item unconsumed, the first poll consumes it itself and returns false; the next poll sees an empty queue and passes. Thus the test repairs the exact unconsumed-input defect it claims to detect. Inspect persisted consumption without changing it, and verify that the runtime consumer processed the item.
findings.title: Not done: settings-reload consumption test

findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

The replacement active-turn path routes every non-command message through buildLiveTurnContinuation, including messages carrying responseSchema or agentControls. That builder emits only formatted text and routing metadata (live-turn-continuation.ts:37–43), so these request settings disappear while the item remains consumed. The removed message-loop path explicitly closed stdin and queued a fresh turn for such messages. Restore an equivalent boundary so controlled requests reach runAgent with their settings.
findings.title: Keep requests with schema or model controls out of plain continuations

findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

A successful handled result does not necessarily mean every taken message was handled. In session/session-commands.ts:366–370, a pre-command run that outputs and then fails returns success=true after advancing only past the preceding messages, deliberately leaving the command pending. This branch now keeps the entire batch consumed, including that unexecuted command, so the next wakeup cannot execute it. Track the handled subset and release the pending command without replaying the already-answered messages.
findings.title: Leave an unexecuted session command available after partial failure
